bug(#7895): stop labeling an application that reads its own receiver

"purify.xsl" widened what counts as data in a part of an application:
besides a copy of data, a part whose row of "links.xml" points at
something the tables call data - a formation that returns a number, a
void witnessed as one - now counted too. The question, though, is put to
the parts alone, and the receiver of an application written as "ξ.name"
is not one of them. "chunk.get" is "read 0 size", whose parts are a
literal and a "size" that returns a number, so the label went onto an
atom that reads a block of memory, and "PhSticky" answered every later
read of that block with the bytes of the first one. Reads of a chunk
stopped seeing writes, and with them "malloc", "while" and every loop
over a tuple: 13 of the ".eo" tests of "eo-runtime" failed in the
"codecov" build, the only one that runs them, since "mvn" and "fast"
build with "eo.transpileTests=false".

The same evidence put the label on 136 more applications of the
standard library, among them ones in "file", "directory", "stdout" and
"socket", so the widening goes back out until "eo:applied" asks what
the receiver of such an application is. The puzzle says so, the pack
that asserted the widened behaviour is replaced by one that pins the
hole it left open, and the reading of the tables that came with it -
the "eo:void" key and the two functions - goes with it.

fix(#7695): compare bytes by content, never by the wrapper's delegate (#7794)

`BytesOf.equals` and `BytesOf.hashCode` delegated to the wrapped
object. `Bytes` is a public interface, so an implementation of it is
free to inherit the identity-based `Object.equals`. Wrapping such an
object made equality asymmetric against `BytesRaw`, which compares
`take()` contents: `raw.equals(wrapped)` was true while
`wrapped.equals(raw)` was false, and the two hash codes differed even
though both held the same single byte. Callers could not put `Bytes`
into a `HashSet` or a `HashMap`, and equality depended on construction
history rather than on byte content.

`BytesOf` now compares and hashes its own `take()` contents, the same
way `BytesRaw` does, so equality is value-based and symmetric whether
the instance came from a `byte[]` or from another `Bytes`. Behaviour of
`BytesOf(byte[])` is unchanged: it delegated to `BytesRaw`, which
already compared the same contents.

fix(#7407): make a copy a snapshot of the origin's empty attributes (#7493)

* fix(#7407): make a copy a snapshot of the origin's empty attributes

`CopiedAttrs` kept a live reference to the origin's attributes and
copied one out only on the first read of it. `Attribute.copy` of a
bound `AtVoid` carries the value bound at that moment, so what a copy
held was decided by when the copy was first read and not by when
`copy()` was called: reading the copy before a late `put` on the origin
gave a terminator, reading it after gave the origin's value.

An empty attribute is the only part of an object whose content can
still change after the copy is made, so only the empty ones are copied
eagerly now, and everything else stays lazy. The scan is bounded: an
attribute never becomes empty again once it is filled, so a copy's own
`taken` already holds every attribute of its that could still be empty,
and a copy of a copy looks no further than that. `Bindings.each` walks
the pairs without building the map that `entrySet` builds.

#6388: stop caging values that depend on the receiver

The `!` marker doesn't just memoize an attribute within one instance —
it eagerly dataizes the expression into raw bytes right where it's
declared (`x.y > z!` compiles to `(Φ.dataized ξ.x.y).as-bytes`, not a
lazy reference). Every one of the new engine's `!`-marked locals
depended, directly or through a chain of other `!`-marked locals, on
`^` (the receiver) or a void parameter, and forcing that chain during
canonical formatting or copying — before the receiver a given call is
actually made through was necessarily the one bound — is what made
`compile.opens` (and everything downstream of it) fail on every single
pattern, valid or not.

None of the new code actually needs memoization for correctness, so
this drops the `!` everywhere it was added and lets these stay the
plain, lazily-resolved references the rest of the object graph already
uses.

feat(lowering): #8137 fold all-literal fragments through phino

An expression decided by data alone, such as "1.plus 1", pays the
full object-graph cost at runtime for a value the compiler could
know. The new "lower" goal, running between merge and transpile,
computes such fragments through the external phino binary and
splices the values back into XMIR as literals.

The new eo-lowering module wraps the binary (pinned to 0.0.112),
renders a fragment into a self-contained phi document with the
number/bytes method tables, and names the result forma after the
outermost of the 12 primitive dispatches. The goal is on by
default and skips with a warning when phino is absent;
eo.loweringRequired turns that skip into a failure, which is what
CI does on Linux. Whether lowering ran is folded into the
transpile cache key through the 4-lower/lowering.txt marker, so
builds with and without phino never share a generated-Java slot.

bug(#7836): read attributes off nodes instead of querying documents

Every rule of the checker asked its questions of the whole document:
an XPath over a ten-megabyte table costs the same four seconds whether
one row comes back or forty thousand do, and a per-node XPath costs
about seventy microseconds against thirty-seven thousand objects on
every pass of the fixed point.

Now the rules walk the tables once and read the attributes off the
nodes they are standing on. Noted is the one way an attribute is read,
Rows the one way a table is walked, Site the one way a dispatch is
asked where it is written and which name it takes.

On the eo-runtime corpus, one hundred and sixty prepared files and
thirty-seven thousand objects: the inference chain falls from 127.4 to
5.9 seconds and the HTML report from 28.2 to 2.9 seconds. Both the
tables and the pages come out byte-identical, and the coverage is
unchanged.

`InetAddrSyscall` and `InetAddrFuncCall` read their address with
`Dataized.asString()` and handed it to a C-string API, which stops at the
first NUL, so `"127.0.0.1\0suffix"` was converted as `"127.0.0.1"` and the
program acted on an address it never named. They were the last two
string-taking native adapters bypassing `Cstring`; #7570 left them out
while the address parsing was being reworked. Both now take the address
through `Cstring`, the way `unlink`, `open`, `getenv` and the rest already
do, and each has the NUL case held by a test.

fix(#8236): check the regex flag section before splicing it in

`compile` took whatever stood after the closing slash and put it between
`(?` and `)` unchecked, so a literal whose flag section carries regex
syntax closed that group and injected its own. `"/b/i)|(?:a"` ran as
`(?i)|(?:a)b`, matched the empty string and said nothing, while `matches`,
which re-reads the literal with `[dimsux]*`, died with "Matched block does
not exist". The flag section is now read with the same alphabet the EO half
uses, and a section that does not fit comes back through `cant-compile`,
naming the flags rather than the internals of `match`.

bug(#8231): a void filled one way teaches the dispatches

Where every call site in the program puts the same object into a void, the
dispatches rooted at that void can be answered concretely instead of
stopping at the void name. Promotion is asked inside the settling loop,
only when the dispatches have nothing left to say, so a void named this
way reopens the dispatches and a dispatch answered may name the next
void. Nothing of it reaches links.xml: what fills a void is a fact about
its callers, so the voids are written down as the rules wrote them.

feat(lowering): #8137 reduce symbolic fragments into protocols

Phino 0.0.114 shipped dataize --partial (phino#1060): atoms stuck on
symbolic inputs park in the evaluation records instead of failing the
run. Reduction now morphs a fragment with its voids rendered as marker
carriers, folds every fired record back into its tree, mints one
protocol step per parked record, and iterates until the tree is a
single value. Atom knowledge stays in phino; the only table on this
side is ops.tsv, keyed by the lambda names phino reports, and whatever
does not settle is refused, so a refusal filters a fragment out
instead of breaking the build.

fix(#8228): follow links while hashing a directory

`Sha` called a path a directory with `Files.isDirectory`, which looks
through a link, and then walked it without `FOLLOW_LINKS`, which does not.
A link to a directory was therefore visited and never entered: no file fed
the digest, so every such path hashed to the digest of empty input and
nothing behind the link ever changed it. A `Cache` keyed by that hash kept
serving output built from contents that had moved on. The walk now looks
through links too, the way the two tests of the path already do.

fix(#8226): drop the catalog cache when the catalog file goes

`Catalogs` keys its map by path alone, so the entry outlives the file.
`MjRegister` deletes the foreign catalog before rebuilding it, but the
`TjCached` for that path stayed in the process-wide map, and a second
`eo:register` in the same Maven JVM started from the rows it had just
removed. Sources deleted between the two runs stayed registered, and later
goals parsed and resolved them as if they still existed. `Catalogs.drop`
now forgets a path, and `removeOldFiles` says so after the deletion.

bug(#8278): take a name written alone off the object around it

A name written by itself means the same as a name written after a dot, and
the parser writes no receiver beside it, so the receiver void it fills had
nothing to witness it and every body reading through a caret stayed rooted
at an empty void. Taken gathers both kinds into the one map Bound already
reads, and it reads the links table for the owner instead of walking
outwards a second time, since a second walk is a second chance to disagree
with the first.

bug(#8281): leave the caret out of the receivers

What a caret takes is the receiver of the object below it, and that object
is not what fills it: the caret of an oak comes from whoever took the oak,
so it is the caller's caller and never the oak itself. Recording the
caret's own receiver as the filling put the object one step too far in and
left the void with two answers that disagree, which is one predicate on the
XPath to fix.

The codecov build folds all-literal fragments through phino and demands
lowering, so `(0.div 0).as-bytes` in the number tests came back as the
bytes phino printed: on an x86 host a zero-by-zero division sets the
sign bit of its NaN, giving FF-F8-00-00-00-00-00-00, while EO knows a

computed NaN into that very object. The folded literal thus stopped

only where lowering runs. A Datum whose last atom answered with a
number now hands out the canonical bytes for any NaN bit pattern and
keeps everything else, infinities included, exactly as printed.

fix(maven-plugin): #8295 merge package members before transpiling

A downstream project that compiles the objects of `eo-runtime` with
`register`, `compile` and `transpile`, the goals the plugin's README
documents, produced Java that `javac` refused: the generated
`org/eolang/EO_string/EOregex.java` named `EOregex$EOcompile` and
`EOregex$EOpattern$EOmatch$EOmatched_from_index`, and no such classes
exist in that package.

They exist in `org.eolang`, as `EOstring$EOregex$EOcompile` and
`EOstring$EOregex$EOpattern$EOmatch$EOmatched_from_index`, which is
where an atom of `string.regex` belongs once `regex` is an attribute
of `string`. The `merge` goal puts it there, but only `eo-runtime`
names that goal, so a build that skipped it compiled `regex` as an
object of its own in an `EO_string` package and named atoms nobody
ships.

`MjTranspile` now merges on its own, before it writes anything, since
it is the goal that turns the shape of an object into class names.
`Merging` indexes the tojos that are standalone rather than every tojo
with XMIR, so a member already inside its object is not moved a second
time and naming the `merge` goal as well, the way `eo-runtime` does
before `inference` and `lower`, still costs nothing.

fix(lowering): #8137 save sidecar bodies atomically

The passes run in parallel across the XMIRs of one build, so two
fragments with the same digest could write one sidecar path at once,
and a plain Files.write would let one of them leave a truncated file.
The body now streams into a sibling temporary file and is renamed into
place atomically by the new Sidecar class, which both Lowered and
Outlined delegate to; a target that already exists is left alone,
since its digest name vouches for its content.

fix(maven): #7945 drop the puzzle the rows key already answered

The transpile cache key folds the rows of the objects one file holds,
and `Transpiling` derives the cache of a tojo from that segment and
hands it to `JavaFiles`, so the generated Java is keyed by the rows
too, which `JavaFilesTest.missesTheJavaFileCachedUnderAnotherKey`
pins. The puzzle asking for it stayed behind and says the opposite of
what the code does, so it goes, and the javadoc says where the Java
files get their key.

fix(rultor): #8295 install phino as root

The release of `0.63.1` died twice at the `install` step with
`curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination`, right after `pdd`
finished reading the sources. Rultor runs the build script as the
unprivileged user `r`, and `/usr/local/bin` belongs to root, so curl
could neither create the output file nor could `chmod` follow. The
reason stayed invisible because `--silent` also silences the
`Failed to open the file ...: Permission denied` warning that curl
prints before it gives up; `--no-progress-meter` keeps that warning
and drops only the progress bar.
